subject: chemistry
question_text: Among the following pairs of orbitals which orbital will experience the larger effective nuclear charge? (i) 2s and 3s, (ii) 4d and 4f, (iii) 3d and 3p
answer_text: Nuclear charge is defined as the net positive charge experienced by an electron in the orbital of a multi-electron atom. The closer the orbital, the greater is the nuclear charge experienced by the electron(s) in it. (i) The electron(s) present in the 2s orbital will experience greater nuclear charge (being closer to the nucleus) than the electron(s) in the 3s orbital. (ii) 4d will experience greater nuclear charge than 4f since 4d is closer to the nucleus. (iii) 3p will experience greater nuclear charge since it is closer to the nucleus than 3f.
final_answer: Thus, the order of effective nuclear charge experienced is: 2s > 3d > 4d > 4f.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of nuclear charge and electron configuration.

subject: chemistry
question_text: The unpaired electrons in Al and Si are present in 3p orbital. Which electrons will experience more effective nuclear charge from the nucleus?
answer_text: Nuclear charge is defined as the net positive charge experienced by an electron in a multi-electron atom. The higher the atomic number, the higher is the nuclear charge. Silicon has 14 protons while aluminium has 13 protons. Hence, silicon has a larger nuclear charge of (+14) than aluminium, which has a nuclear charge of (+13). Thus, the electrons in the 3p orbital of silicon will experience a more effective nuclear charge than aluminium.
final_answer: Therefore, the electrons in silicon's 3p orbital experience a greater effective nuclear charge.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of atomic structure and nuclear charge.

parts.part_text: Iron (Fe): Atomic number = 26. The electronic configuration is: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2 3d6. From the orbital picture, iron has four unpaired electrons.

parts.part_text: Krypton (Kr): Atomic number = 36. The electronic configuration is: 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 4s2 3d10 4p6. Since all orbitals are fully occupied, there are no unpaired electrons in krypton.
